prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2015 manifesto centres on a “Budget Responsibility Lock”: every policy is fully funded without extra borrowing; the deficit will be cut every year, with debt falling and a current budget surplus as soon as possible; and major parties’ manifestos will be OBR-audited. It pledges fairer taxes (restore 50p top rate, a new 10p starting rate funded by scrapping the Marriage Allowance, no rises to basic/higher Income Tax, NI or VAT, abolish non-dom status) and a clampdown on avoidance. Spending cuts exclude health, education and international development.

Economy and work: A long-term industrial strategy to raise productivity, with a National Infrastructure Commission, support for HS2 and northern rail links, roads and cycling, and a swift airports decision post-Davies. Back a million green jobs, decarbonise electricity by 2030, empower the Green Investment Bank, and expand broadband/mobile coverage. Create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; cut and then freeze business rates for 1.5m small firms; boost banking competition and levy payday lenders. Raise the minimum wage to over £8 by Oct 2019, promote the Living Wage via procurement and “Make Work Pay” contracts, ban exploitative zero-hours contracts (right to a regular contract after 12 weeks), close agency-worker loopholes, and scrap employment tribunal fees.

Skills and youth: Guarantee an apprenticeship for every qualified school leaver; require major government contractors and large non-EU recruiters to offer apprenticeships; create employer-led Technical Degrees and a gold-standard Technical Baccalaureate; cut university tuition fees to £6,000; introduce a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee funded by a bank bonus tax; replace 18–21 out-of-work benefits with a Youth Allowance tied to training.

Markets and bills: Freeze energy prices until 2017, empower the regulator to cut bills, split Big Six generation/supply, simplify tariffs, and deliver mass home energy efficiency. Reform water affordability. Rail: allow a public operator, establish a national rail body, freeze fares next year and cap future rises; devolve bus powers and smart ticketing.

NHS and care: Fund 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 GPs and 3,000 midwives via a Mansion Tax on £2m+ properties, a tobacco levy and anti-avoidance; 48-hour GP appointments and one-week cancer tests by 2020; repeal the Health and Social Care Act, cap private profits, integrate physical, mental and social care, and give mental health parity (28-day access to talking therapies). End 15-minute care visits; recruit 5,000 home-care workers; support carers.

Education: Protect the whole education budget; all teachers qualified; new School Leadership Institute; Directors of School Standards to intervene locally; end the Free Schools programme; cap infant class sizes at 30; strengthen vocational routes; compulsory, age-appropriate sex and relationships education.

Housing and social security: Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020, back small builders and garden cities, “use it or lose it” on land, first call for local first-time buyers; private renting reform with three-year tenancies, caps on excessive rent rises, a ban on letting fees and a landlord register; abolish the Bedroom Tax; keep a benefits cap; tailor back-to-work support; reform the Work Capability Assessment; higher JSA for long contributors; pause and review Universal Credit.

Immigration and communities: 1,000 extra border staff (funded by a small charge on non-visa visitors), full exit checks, tighter short-term student visas, no EU benefits for two years, English requirement for public-facing roles, ban agencies recruiting solely from overseas, extend the Gangmasters Authority; humane enforcement and end indefinite detention for pregnant women and abuse victims.

Safety, rights and culture: Protect neighbourhood policing (safeguard 10,000 officers), abolish PCCs, create a Police Standards Authority, a Victims’ Law, tougher action on VAWG with a commissioner and stable refuge funding, ban “legal highs,” expand restorative justice. Overhaul Prevent, restore stronger terror controls with oversight, zero tolerance of hate crime. Require gender pay gap reporting; race equality strategy; advance LGBT rights; protect the Human Rights Act; extend FOI to large private providers; repeal and replace the Lobbying Act; ban MPs’ paid directorships.

Devolution and democracy: Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; English Devolution Act transferring £30bn and powers over transport, skills and housing; empower communities over high streets; implement further devolution to Scotland and Wales; votes at 16.

Europe and the world: Remain in and reform the EU for jobs and growth, with a referendum lock on any future power transfers; NATO commitment; SDSR in year one; uphold the armed forces covenant (veterans’ support, anti-discrimination law); maintain a minimum, credible nuclear deterrent; strengthen cyber security. Lead on climate diplomacy (net zero global emissions in the second half of the century). Keep 0.7% aid, focus on the poorest, create a Centre for Universal Health Coverage, tackle tax avoidance and modern slavery in supply chains.
